title: Army Dog Tyson Receives Presidential Honor After Taking Bullet in J&K Counter-Terror Operation
excerpt: The German Shepherd, attached to 2 Para Special Forces, was shot while leading troops to a terrorist hideout in Kishtwar and has been awarded a Mention-in-Despatches on Independence Day.
body:
• Army assault dog Tyson, a German Shepherd attached to 2 Para Special Forces, has been awarded a Mention-in-Despatches by President Droupadi Murmu on Independence Day 2026.
  • Tyson was shot in the leg while leading troops to a hidden terrorist hideout during Operation Trashi-I in Kishtwar, Jammu and Kashmir, on February 22.
  • Despite his injury, the dog pressed forward and confirmed the location of three Pakistan-sponsored terrorists, all of whom were neutralized by security forces.
  • Tyson is the only animal among the 89 personnel chosen for the honor this year.

A Bullet Could Not Stop Tyson

Indian Army assault dog Tyson has been awarded a Mention-in-Despatches by President Droupadi Murmu for "bravery and extraordinary courage" during a counter-insurgency operation in Jammu and Kashmir earlier this year, making him the only animal among 89 personnel honored on Independence Day 2026.

https://x.com/AskAnshul/status/2088687017874133057

The German Shepherd, part of the elite canine unit attached to 2 Para Special Forces, was shot in the leg while leading troops into a suspected terrorist hideout during Operation Trashi-I in the Chatroo belt of Kishtwar district on February 22. Despite the wound, Tyson continued to advance, confirming the precise location of the concealed militants.

"Tyson displayed extraordinary courage by taking the first bullet while leading the entry into the terrorists' hideout. Undeterred by his injuries, he pressed forward and launched a fierce assault, compelling the terrorists to open fire and thereby confirming their presence."

— Indian Army, White Knight Corps statement on X

Operation Trashi-I: Three Terrorists Neutralized

The encounter in Kishtwar's Chatroo forest began when intelligence gathered by J&K Police, the Intelligence Bureau and Army sources pinpointed the movement of militants in the area. A joint operation was launched, with Tyson scouting ahead of the troops to locate a hidden terrorist hideout.

As the unit advanced, concealed militants opened fire. Tyson took the first bullet but continued moving forward toward the entry point, drawing hostile fire away from the soldiers and revealing the terrorists' exact positions. His actions enabled troops from the White Knight Corps, J&K Police and CRPF to engage and neutralize all three Pakistan-sponsored terrorists, including a senior Jaish-e-Muhammad commander.

The Army described the operation as "a perfect example of perseverance, clarity of thought and seamless coordination at all levels." Officials noted that the mission was accomplished without any casualties among the soldiers — Tyson was the only one injured.

Recovery and Recognition

After being wounded, Tyson was airlifted to Command Hospital Udhampur for emergency veterinary treatment. The Army confirmed he has since made a full recovery.

"Wounded yet in high spirits, alert and recovering well, Tyson exemplifies unwavering devotion to duty, a true warrior and a soldier in every sense."

— Indian Army statement

A Mention-in-Despatches is an official military commendation recognizing bravery and meritorious service in a combat zone. While recipients do not receive a gallantry medal, they earn an official certificate and the right to wear a specific emblem on their campaign medal ribbon.

Military Dogs on the Frontlines

Tyson's honor follows a growing recognition of the role canine units play in India's counter-terrorism operations. In January 2025, another Army dog, Phantom from 9 Para Special Forces, was posthumously awarded a Mention-in-Despatches after being killed during an operation in the Akhnoor sector of Jammu and Kashmir.

Military working dogs are used in situations where human soldiers would face immediate danger, including locating hidden terrorists, detecting explosives, and establishing enemy positions in confined spaces. German Shepherds like Tyson are selected for their intelligence, agility and ability to remain calm under fire.

The Independence Day honor formally acknowledges what frontline commanders have long known: in the most dangerous moments of combat, these four-legged soldiers are often the first through the door.
nri_angle: The story of Army dog Tyson's bravery during a counter-terror operation resonated with the Indian diaspora, drawing widespread attention on India's 80th Independence Day.
